title: Concept: Access-Control-Allow-Origin uses a wildcard inside an origin
description: Access-Control-Allow-Origin carries a scheme and host pattern with a wildcard character in it. The CORS protocol only permits the literal * or one exact origin, so the browser matches nothing, credentialed cross-origin reads fail, and the policy records an origin-sharing intent it does not implement.
risk: The CORS policy silently fails or reflects too widely, depending on how the value is generated; LOW severity because the common outcome is a broken grant.
